To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a simple instance search tracker can be built upon a learned Siamese matching function, (2) this matching function can be trained generically, and (3) the tracker built upon this matching function can track previously unseen targets and re-identify them after they are temporarily absent from the scene.
a Siamese neural network can be trained to learn a powerful matching function for instance search and that this function can be used to build a simple tracker, which outperforms the state-of-the-art.

a) a deep neural network trained generically on many different targets can be used to track a previously unseen target, and b) a simple tracker built on top of this matching function suffices to reach the state-of-the-art.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning the matching function for tracking, which is generic and does not need any data of the tracked target.
the fundamental problem of how to learn a matching function that is powerful enough to track a previously unseen target.
the question of whether it is possible to build a tracker that is as simple as possible and still reaches state-of-the-art results.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed tracker is a simple and powerful tracker.
we present the first tracker that is trained generically and then used as is to track previously unseen instances.
we propose a simple, yet powerful, tracker, which does not require any updating or adapting to track a target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose to use Siamese instance search for tracking, which allows us to track without any model updating, occlusion detection, or geometric matching, yet delivers state-of-the-art results.
we present a tracker with a matching function, which is learned to be very discriminative and robust against occlusion, and which is applied without any adaptation to track previously unseen objects.
we propose to learn the entire tracking problem from a generic dataset and then apply the learned matching function without any further training or adapting to track previously unseen objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a learned matching function, which is generic and trained on large-scale data, can replace the need for updating a model and for geometric matching, which are typically used in tracking.

the proposed tracker, SINT, is very simple, yet very effective, and that the proposed training scheme, Siamese Instance Search (SIS), is very effective in learning a powerful matching function, which we believe can be used in many computer vision tasks.
a simple tracker can reach state-of-the art performance if it uses the most powerful generic matching function, which is trained on a large dataset of videos.
